purpose: Seal the People-to-Approval separation-task waiver request and Approval-to-People terminal decision as one purpose-separated atomic bridge so the HRM-013 waiver callback has a provable origin.

existingBridgePattern.reuseRule: Reuse the hardened proof, immutable byte, outbox, lease and receipt principles only. Employee-change endpoints, purpose, tables and workflow bindings are not reusable HRM-013 authority.

operationNaming.rule: operationId is the exact implementation/API identifier; semanticOperation is the immutable HRM-013 contract vocabulary. The CSV source_operation_id, this bridge operationId and the callback authority sourceOperationId must match exactly.

requiredApplicationHeaders.X-DWP-Workload-Proof: exactly one compact certificate-bound RS256 JWS
requiredApplicationHeaders.X-Correlation-ID: exactly one canonical lowercase UUID equal to body and signed claim

headerRules: Authorization bearer authentication is forbidden; the only application proof carrier is X-DWP-Workload-Proof.
Duplicate, additional, transformed, joined, blank or noncanonical application headers fail before replay reservation.
Content-Encoding and Transfer-Encoding transformations are forbidden at the application boundary.

rules: APR-002 exact request bytes in People and Approval request persistence and HRM-010 exact callback body bytes in the Approval decision outbox are each capped at 32768 bytes.
APR-002 submission receipts, HRM-010 SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 receipts and every safe error response are independently capped at 16384 bytes.
A request persistence limit never authorizes a response larger than 16384 bytes, and an oversized request or response fails before its bytes are admitted as durable evidence.
approvalRequestId is generated once by People and is the stable request idempotency identity.
caseMakerPublicId is the immutable case creator and requestedByActorPublicId is the waiver requester; Approval cannot replace either.
taskOwnerRevision and taskVersion are the exact People fence values at request creation and never become caller-supplied People authority.
payloadSha256 binds schemaName=SeparationWaiverApprovalRequestV1, schemaVersion=1 and every other body field under RFC 8785 and excludes only itself.
decisionRevision exactly equals ownerRevision in the body and the signed ownerRevision claim.
originatingPayloadSha256 exactly equals the People waiver-request outbox approval_request_payload_sha256 derived from APR-002 payloadSha256.
APPROVED requires exact body/proof/outbox equality for every step-up field, while REJECTED forbids all step-up fields and claims.

wire.SeparationWaiverDecisionV2.ownerRevision: signed workload-proof ownerRevision and protocol-fence expected_next_owner_revision
wire.SeparationWaiverDecisionV2.decisionRevis: terminal Approval decision sequence for the same approvalRequestId

hrm010RevisionMapping.equalityRule: The two wire values, signed ownerRevision, Approval owner_revision, Approval decision_revision, People owner_revision, People decision_revision and the fence expected_next_owner_revision are all the same positive integer; any mismatch fails before task mutation.
hrm010RevisionMapping.databaseRule: Both V59 and the bounded People V61 prerequisite persistence require an owner_revision = decision_revision check for HRM-010 rows in addition to application validation.

requestCreation: People validates the case and task under trusted tenant context, exact task CAS and a published immutable task template.
People rejects a completed or waived task, an irreversible case, a self-approval policy violation and any missing reason before creating the request.

One People transaction persists ppl_separation_waiver_request_outbox with caseMakerPublicId, requestedByActorPublicId, reasonCode, taskOwnerRevision, taskVersion, exact APR-002 request bytes, requestBodySha256, approval_request_payload_sha256, commandDigest and correlationId under tenantId plus approvalRequestId.
The relay uses the immutable outbox bytes and rotates only its short-lived workload proof on retry.
approvalAdmission: Approval verifies mTLS SPIFFE, closed RS256 claims, certificate confirmation, exact method/path/body hash, signed tenant and current caller grant before request lookup.
Approval atomically reserves jti and requestNonce and then reserves approvalRequestId with the exact command digest.
An exact replay returns the original byte-identical submission receipt; a changed digest returns 409 without creating another request.
Approval resolves an exact published separation-waiver workflow and form revision, freezes the policy revision, persists exact safe request and response bytes, and enters PENDING.
terminalDecision: Only a native terminal APPROVED or REJECTED decision under the frozen workflow produces one immutable decision outbox row.

The terminal accepted vote actor is decisionActorPublicId; Approval proves that actor is different from both caseMakerPublicId and requestedByActorPublicId, and People independently repeats both comparisons from its immutable fence.

APPROVED requires stepUpEvidenceId, stepUpEvidenceAudience, stepUpEvidencePurpose, stepUpEvidenceNonce, stepUpEvidenceDigest, stepUpVerifiedAt and stepUpConsumedAt; Approval verifies freshness and audience/purpose binding and atomically consumes the one-time nonce before terminal decision.
REJECTED requires no step-up evidence and all seven step-up fields and claims are absent rather than null.

Each approvalRequestId has one terminal revision stream: decisionRevision and signed ownerRevision are both 1, callbackEventId is the stable decision event identity, delivery retries are exact no-ops, and a later waiver attempt requires a new approvalRequestId with a new revision-1 stream.
The outbox freezes exact HRM-010 path, body, body hash, command digest and correlation before any delivery attempt.

People admits the callback only when approvalRequestId, case, task, reason, correlation and originatingPayloadSha256 exactly match its immutable request fence, where originatingPayloadSha256 equals approval_request_payload_sha256 derived from APR-002 payloadSha256.
atomicity: Approval terminal state and decision outbox insert commit in one transaction.
People callback evidence, task effect, receipt_public_id, exact safe SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 bytes and audit commit in one transaction.
APPROVED may set WAIVED and READY_TO_PUBLISH only under current task and case CAS; REJECTED records evidence and performs no waiver mutation.
Neither timeout nor ambiguous delivery creates success; RESULT_UNKNOWN requires reconciliation using the same immutable decision event.

jws.certificateConfirmation: cnf.x5t#S256 exactly equals the SHA-256 thumbprint of the validated mTLS leaf certificate

SVC-PEP-HRM-010.decisionRevisionRule: decisionRevision is required in the body but deliberately not duplicated as a JWT claim; it must exactly equal the signed ownerRevision claim.

tenantGrantAuthority.currentRowRule: Load the highest same-tenant grant_revision and require decision=ADMIT; unavailable, ambiguous, stale or revoked authority fails closed.
tenantGrantAuthority.pairBindingRule: One current grant_id row contains the exact APR-002 request binding/purpose and HRM-010 callback binding/purpose plus both workload SPIFFE identities and signing key ids; tenantGrantRevision and authorizationRevision must come from that same row and may never be mixed across revisions.
tenantGrantAuthority.apr002AdmissionRule: Approval verifies both signed revision claims against that current ADMIT row and persists its grant_id plus both revisions with the immutable waiver request binding.
tenantGrantAuthority.hrm010OutboundRule: Terminal decision and outbox creation reuse the same persisted grant_id row, require it still be the current ADMIT row, persist both revision values, and sign the HRM-010 proof with those exact values; delivery fails closed if the row is no longer current.

replayPersistence.rule: The two distinct canonical UUID values are hashed separately and inserted atomically; tenant-scoped digest reuse fails even when binding, caller or token kind differs.

workloadProofProfile.replay: jti and requestNonce are different fresh canonical UUIDs whose separate tenant-scoped token digests are atomically reserved as two rows in the receiving service's one durable replay namespace before owner business facts; reuse under another binding or caller is forbidden.

idempotency.requestDigest: SHA-256 over bindingId, method, exact path, caller, audience, tenant, purpose, content type and exact body SHA-256 in fixed LF-delimited order.
idempotency.sameRequestSameDigest: Return the byte-identical original SeparationWaiverApprovalSubmissionReceiptV1 and do not create another approval request.
idempotency.sameRequestDifferentDigest: 409_EMPTY_NO_STORE without workflow or target existence detail.
idempotency.sameDecisionSameDigest: People returns the byte-identical stored SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 without owner aggregate reads.
idempotency.sameDecisionDifferentDigest: 409_EMPTY_NO_STORE; preserve original callback row and append quarantine audit without aggregate reads.

waiverRequestFence.hrm010OriginRule: SeparationWaiverDecisionV2.originatingPayloadSha256 and its signed claim exactly equal approval_request_payload_sha256.

proofReplay.rule: Derive distinct JTI and REQUEST_NONCE token digests and atomically insert both rows in one namespace before callback fence or aggregate reads; any tenant-scoped digest reuse fails even across binding or caller metadata.

protocolFence.streamNullSemantics: NULLS NOT DISTINCT; approval_request_id is non-null for HRM-010 and null for HRM-008/009.
protocolFence.hrm010Rule: Each approval_request_id is an isolated revision stream: first ownerRevision=decisionRevision=1, its one terminal APPROVED or REJECTED decision closes the stream, and a later waiver request uses a new approvalRequestId and a new revision-1 stream.
protocolFence.grantRevisionRule: tenant_grant_revision and authorization_revision are separate required values from the same current People service-grant row and exactly equal the two HRM-010 signed claims.

requiredChanges: Create apr_hrm013_tenant_grants with append-only ADMIT or REVOKE revisions for exactly APR-002 and HRM-010; do not widen V58 grant semantics.

Create apr_hrm013_proof_replays with tenant_id plus token_digest uniqueness and atomic separate JTI/REQUEST_NONCE rows for APR-002 and HRM-010; do not alter apr_hris_bridge_proof_replays or its V58 allowlist.

Create apr_hrm013_waiver_request_bindings with immutable request bytes capped at 32768, response bytes capped at 16384, their hashes, the exact current grant_id plus separate tenant_grant_revision and authorization_revision, case maker, waiver requester, reason, task revision/version, People identities, frozen workflow/form/policy and idempotency aliases.

Create apr_hrm013_waiver_decision_outbox with immutable callback path/body capped at 32768, receipt capped at 16384, digests, the same current grant_id and two revision values, originatingPayloadSha256, terminal actor, owner/decision revision equality, all seven conditional step-up evidence fields, bounded lease/retry and exact People receipt.
Apply tenant foreign keys, exact uniqueness, digest checks, immutable-source triggers and a bounded claim index.
Perform no seed, tenant enrollment, workflow activation, credential insertion or production binding.
reuse: no V58 HRIS bridge table is widened or reused as HRM-013 persistence
forbidden: editing Approval migrations V1 through V58
reusing employee-change bridge rows or purpose codes

stepUpEvidenceContract.digestEncoding: The eight values are encoded in order as canonical UTF-8 with one LF delimiter and no trailing LF, then SHA-256 lowercase hexadecimal.
approvedRules: Approval validates the evidence issuer, audience, purpose, decision actor and frozen freshness policy, then atomically consumes the unique tenantId plus stepUpEvidenceNonce before committing APPROVED and its outbox.
stepUpVerifiedAt is not after stepUpConsumedAt; stepUpConsumedAt is the terminal decision transaction time and is not after callback occurredAt.
The outbox, HRM-010 body and HRM-010 proof carry exactly the same seven values; People rejects any mismatch or prior use of the evidence identity, nonce or digest.
stepUpEvidenceContract.rejectedRule: REJECTED does not require step-up; all seven fields and claims are absent, explicit null is invalid, and no synthetic evidence is created.

durableOutbox.conditionalStepUpRule: The seven step-up fields are immutable and non-null only for APPROVED; they are absent for REJECTED.
durableOutbox.claim: SKIP_LOCKED bounded batch with lease token and expiry; only the current lease holder may record an attempt outcome.
durableOutbox.delivery: Exact callback bytes, path, callbackEventId and command digest never change; every attempt uses a fresh proof. Every verified success or error response is capped at 16384 bytes.
durableOutbox.receipt: DELIVERED requires a closed valid SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 capped at 16384 bytes whose callbackEventId, type, case, task, revision, correlation and command digest equal the outbox row.

retryContract.responseSizeRule: Any response over 16384 bytes is unverifiable, is never interpreted as success and follows the bounded invalid-receipt retry path.
retryContract.manualReplay: Creates a new delivery attempt receipt linked to the same immutable decision event; it never rewrites decision source bytes.

acceptanceConditions: APR-002 and HRM-010 are a single purpose-separated handshake and neither reuses APR-001 or HRM-001 semantics, rows or purpose.
Only exact People and Approval SPIFFE identities with closed RS256 proofs, signed tenants and current grants cross the two private endpoints.

People creates one immutable ppl_separation_waiver_request_outbox fence under task CAS before submission and preserves case maker, requester, reason, task revision/version, exact request bytes, body digest, approval request payload digest, command digest and correlation.
Approval exact request replay returns the original bytes while a changed body under the same approvalRequestId returns 409.
Approval freezes the exact workflow, form, policy, actors, reason, task versions, payload digest and correlation.

The decision actor differs from both maker and requester; APPROVED requires seven fresh single-use step-up values bound to dwp-people-server and HRIS_SEPARATION_TASK_WAIVER_DECISION, while REJECTED carries none.
Terminal decision and immutable callback outbox commit atomically; request or callback timeouts never invent success.
Approval callback retries preserve exact path/body/event/digest and rotate only the proof; receipt mismatch remains retryable then RESULT_UNKNOWN.

People validates exact request lineage and originatingPayloadSha256 before WAIVED; decisionRevision equals signed ownerRevision, REJECTED never waives and APPROVED cannot override irreversible evidence.
Every APR-002 and HRM-010 success or error response is at most 16384 bytes.
Approval V59 and bounded People V61 prerequisite persistence remain unreserved and source remains withheld until separate authorities, worktree receipts, exclusive leases and hash-bound tokens.
nonClaims: Approval V59 or the bounded People V61 prerequisite persistence is reserved, leased, authored or executed.
A production workflow, form, key, certificate, service grant, tenant or callback sender is configured.
The existing employee-change bridge authorizes separation waiver traffic.
The HRM-013 owner packet, People V61 lease, module worktree or module token is authorized.
A separation task can currently be waived through runtime Approval.
